# #197 round 3 correctness review: PASS-WITH-NOTES

Head: `1894c36072158cd3c1e85a4c49db8fcc027aeaf3`.
Request: `01a1beb0-08d8-77e2-8c9b-0d61231c0791`.
Final C34 review of F003-F005, separating repair `cf43a115` from inherited main `3e312437`. Detached worktree clean and pinned. No local builds, tests or live probes.

**All three normal-use blockers are closed.**

## F003: Atomic local Telegram admission

`SqliteBackground::settle_by_telegram` updates the orphan record, inserts the Telegram job and marks the background job notified within one `begin_write` transaction, owned through completion (`crates/store/src/background.rs:764-820`). Failure rolls back the record and mark along with the queue operation. The separate pre-enqueue commitment and ignored undo are gone.

Production composition gives the real queue and background store the same persistent pool (`crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:420-428,456-462,594-595`). The daemon supplies the ordinary Telegram job built by `send_job`; the real sidecar can claim that row. The store test forces queue insertion failure and verifies unchanged record, no mark and no row, then verifies all three on retry. The daemon test exercises a pre-transaction failure and braked retry. Another test claims/ACKs the real SQLite Telegram row, then confirms further ticks enqueue nothing.

This closes the rejected “lose one Telegram, never double” trade at the local admission boundary. It does not claim exactly-once Telegram network transport.

## F004: Settlement before tail IO; tail failures braked

Saved settlement and current owner classification now precede `final_body`. Orphans and recorded/admitted settlement retries do not reopen an unused log. A present-owner tail-read failure records the next look 60 seconds out before returning its error.

The new fixtures exercise both Done and timed-out jobs with missing logs, not only Lost jobs: present-owner failure is braked, a gone owner settles without the tail, and an admitted settlement finishes after its log disappears without a second notice. The SQL skip filter remains the only tick brake, preventing waiting-row hydration.

## F005: Admission evidence after an ambiguous accept error

After `accept` errors, the prime leg now reads `delivery.admitted` again before recording any fallback. Positive admission keeps the prime route; negative admission permits fallback; a failed lookup retains the route and returns the error through `settle_braked`, rather than treating uncertainty as refusal.

The tests inject audit publication failure after admission and verify no Telegram plus a settled job. A scripted failure of the admission recheck leaves the route Prime and the job unmarked/braked; recovery settles without redelivery. Earlier owner-revive, gone-prime and cold-prime replay cases also passed.
